passage:
A family installed a smart door lock that opened with a phone. They no longer needed keys.
One day, the phone battery died while the family was outside. Luckily, they had kept a backup key with a neighbor.
The father said the lock was convenient, but convenience should not remove every backup.
The family also changed their password after learning that weak passwords could create risks.
The smart lock made entering easier, but it did not end responsibility.
A new tool often solves an old problem while creating new rules. The question is not only whether something is smart, but whether the people using it are prepared.
